instruction: Go to the second slide and add the title "Digital Marketplace" in blue color (RGB: 0, 0, 255).

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Variation requires adding a title with a different color (blue instead of red), testing color specification ability. Blue color RGB(0,0,255) explicitly specified in instruction.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.5 for correct title text, 0.5 for correct color, 1.0 for both correct

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Getter logic is non-deterministic - iterates through all shapes and returns FIRST non-empty text found, not specifically targeting the title placeholder. May extract subtitle/content text instead of actual slide title.

CRITICAL: Color extraction logic is incorrect - python-pptx RGBColor object is accessed as rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2] but should use rgb.r, rgb.g, rgb.b attributes. This will cause runtime AttributeError.
MINOR: Expected value uses list [0, 0, 255] while getter returns tuple (0, 0, 255) - semantically inconsistent though Python comparison works.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Update getter to specifically target title placeholder: Check shape.is_placeholder and shape.placeholder_format.type == PP_PLACEHOLDER.TITLE (or similar), or check shape.has_text_frame and shape.name for title-specific names.
Fix color extraction: Change 'rgb = run.font.color.rgb' and access as '(rgb.r, rgb.g, rgb.b)' instead of 'rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2]'.
Standardize expected value format to match getter output (use tuple instead of list for color).
Add edge case handling: Check if shape.text_frame exists before accessing, verify run.font.color is not None before extracting RGB.
